method: structural walk + musical known-plaintext (file is Beethoven's Symphony No. 5 opening; pitches G4=67/G3=55/G2=43, Eb, F, D stacks confirm raw-MIDI pitch field) + Rosetta cross-ref to ANSI-Music/IGS text protocol (DEVO3.IG n> events use the same raw-MIDI pitch space, e.g. Whip It riff 62=D4, 38=D2)

container.rule: one or more `N>1,<len>,` headers (first may carry G# prefix); each header followed by exactly <len> bytes of event stream; chunks concatenate into ONE continuous stream; a 6-byte record may straddle a chunk boundary with the next N> header spliced between its halves

note_event_6B.status: 0x90..0x94, low nibble = channel (all 1069 attacks use 0x90; 0x92-0x94 appear only as pitch-0 marker events)
note_event_6B.f1: flag 0/1, unresolved (differs between a note's attack and release, so NOT a voice id)
note_event_6B.pitch: raw MIDI note number 36..87, 0 = silence marker
note_event_6B.dur: 0x57 (87) on every note attack, 0x00 on every release (attack/release discriminator)
note_event_6B.delta: ticks until next event, 0..255 observed (post-attached; delta 255 = fermata holds)

record_grammar.compressed_4B: [status, f1, dur, delta] with pitch/f3 inherited from previous event; observed exactly once, at the chunk-1/chunk-2 boundary (offset 9996): decodes as a G4 re-articulation
record_grammar.control_events: 0xC0..0xD0, 4-byte [cN,0,0,x] and 10-byte forms; 17 consecutive codes c0..d0 at end of file; semantics open (MIDI-like program-change analogy is a hypothesis)

validation.beethoven5_opening_check: first 12 attacks = 67,55,43 x3 (G octave stacks) then 51,39,63 (Eb stack) then F stack 53,41,65 then D stack 62,50,38 with 255-tick fermatas between - matches Symphony No.5 i. Allegro con brio opening
validation.musical_coherence: staggered chord attacks (1-tick voice spacing), 20-21 tick short notes, 255-tick fermatas, octave-alternating bass G2/G3 in the development - all coherent

DEVO3.IG.identification: Devo 'Whip It' synth riff (62=D4 69=A4 71=B4 67=G4 72=C5 over D2=38/A2=45 bass) - proves text pitch = raw MIDI, same space as .igm binary

rosetta_text_side.alignment_conclusion: text and binary music share the raw-MIDI pitch space and small-int tick deltas; text n> carries explicit inst/slot/vol where binary carries status nibble + f1/f3 flags and constant dur=0x57; no byte-for-byte text<->binary pair exists in the corpus (only one .igm file), so mapping is semantic, not cipher-keyed

open_questions: meaning of f1/f3 flags (f1=1 on 57/1069 attacks; middle release of a chord often f1=1)
meaning of the 0x92-0x94 pitch-0 marker events (70x; channel nibble 2-4 only)
semantics of 0xC0-0xD0 control events (c0..d0 table at EOF; 4B and 10B forms)
delta unit vs the dur=0x57 constant (dur may be a velocity or PSG envelope period, not ticks)
77 releases whose attack was not found (compressed-event pitch inheritance and/or pre-boundary voices)
0x91 never observed; whether more N>1,<len> args exist (arg1 always '1')
only ONE .igm sample in corpus - grammar needs confirmation on more files (discmaster lists ~46 IGS files)
